paraphrase: The channels constantly carry the breath and have the moon, sun and fire as deities; iḍā, piṅgalā and suṣumnā are the three (chief). Prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna and vyāna, and nāga, kūrma, kṛkara, devadatta and dhanañjaya — these ten breaths, in the form of the living soul, move in the thousands of channels.

paraphrase: The three channels iḍā, piṅgalā and suṣumṇā carry the breath and have moon, sun and fire as deities; ten breaths — prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, vyāna, nāga, kūrma, kṛkara, devadatta and dhanañjaya — move in them. Under the sway of prāṇa and apāna the jīva runs up and down, like a ball struck by a bat or a hawk tied by a string; prāṇa draws apāna and apāna draws prāṇa — one who knows this knows yoga.

paraphrase: The living soul, under the control of prāṇa and apāna, runs down and up by the left and right paths and, being restless, is not seen; like a ball struck to the ground bouncing up, like a falcon tied by a cord pulled back, the soul is dragged by prāṇa and apāna; apāna pulls prāṇa and prāṇa pulls apāna — who knows these two, above and below, knows yoga.

paraphrase: The yogīs know the anāhata centre in the heart, where the bull bound threefold roars loudly; passing anāhata and maṇipūra, when the breath reaches the great lotus the yogī becomes immortal; the pure one free of sound (the haṃsa) is known at the throat centre called viśuddha.

paraphrase: In the yogī whose body is filled with nectar the seed flows upward after two or three years and the powers beginning with minuteness arise; as fire with fuel and a lamp with oil and wick, so the embodied one filled with the moon-digit does not leave the body.

paraphrase: Concentration (dhāraṇā) is holding the mind still on the five elements separately: earth (yellow, square, with the syllable la) in the heart, water (crescent, white, va) at the throat, fire (triangular, red, ra) at the palate, air (smoky, round, ya) between the brows, space (clear, ha, with Sadāśiva) in the brahmarandhra; they stabilise, dissolve, burn, whirl and dry, and space-concentration breaks open the door of liberation.

paraphrase: When the mind is fixed on a principle, that is meditation; it is of two kinds, with qualities (distinguished by colour) and without qualities (the alone).

paraphrase: Gazing at the tip of the nose, the yogī meditates on the root centre like molten gold, svādhiṣṭhāna like a ruby, maṇipūra like the rising sun, the heart-lotus like lightning, the throat, the point between the brows like a pearl, and the attributeless, peaceful Śiva in the sky facing all ways; meditating on the self as stainless, sky-like and all-pervading he attains yoga — these places of meditation, joined to adjunct and principle, bring the eight powers.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Gorakṣaśataka, ed. Swami Kuvalayananda and S. A. Shukla (Lonavla: Kaivalyadhama); GRETIL e-text); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.
speaker: Gorakṣa

paraphrase: Adjunct and principle: the adjunct is colour, the principle is the self; the adjunct is wrong knowledge, the principle abides otherwise; as a crystal appears coloured by what is near it, so the self — freed by practice from all adjuncts — is praised; the knowers of the principle know it as fearless, supportless, without elaboration, without resting-place, without disease and formless.

paraphrase: Meditation lasts as long as the five sense-qualities beginning with sound are remembered; beyond that is samādhi. When the breath is exhausted and the mind dissolves, that oneness of equal taste (samarasa) is called samādhi.

paraphrase: The yogin joined in samādhi knows neither smell, taste, form, touch nor sound, neither himself nor another; he is not devoured by time, not bound by karma, not overpowered by anyone. Stainless, unmoving, eternal, actionless, qualityless, great, consciousness of space, bliss — this the knowers of Brahman know as Brahman.

paraphrase: The knowers of Brahman know Brahman as stainless, motionless, eternal, actionless, attributeless, great, sky-like knowledge and bliss; like milk poured into milk, ghee into ghee and fire into fire, the knower of yoga attains non-duality (advayatva) in the supreme state.
